answer: Over the 1991-2015 balanced window of the supplied World Development Indicators panel, a 1-percentage-point rise in Adjusted savings: education expenditure (percentage of GNI) is associated with substantially faster growth in per-capita income (GNI per capita, constant 2015 US$) in Lower-Middle-Income developing countries (LMC) than in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSF/SSA). The comparison comes from a pooled OLS of the change in log GNI per capita - the largest fully balanced sub-sample, since SSA's GNI per capita is observed only from 2011 and differencing then truncates the SSA sample to N = 4 versus N = 24 for LMC, with controls for Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth), Labor force participation rate (modeled ILO estimate), School enrollment primary (gross percent), School enrollment secondary (gross percent), group fixed effects, and Newey-West HAC standard errors: the additional semi-elasticity for LMC versus SSA is +0.078 log-GNI points per +1 percentage-point of education-expenditure share (NW SE 0.050, two-sided p = 0.12), implying a positive semi-elasticity for LMC of about +0.046 and a marginally negative one for SSA of -0.032. The interaction is positive and sign-stable across the winsorized-exports re-run that neutralises the SSA exports-growth outliers of 1999 and 2011 (+0.075, p = 0.15) and across the levels-with-lagged-DV robustness specification that absorbs persistence directly (+0.088, p = 0.087, with the lagged log GNI coefficient at 0.90). This is best read as a conditional association rather than a causal elasticity: the dataset aggregates two country groups (SSA and LMC) with no external instrument for Adjusted savings: education expenditure, the SSA GNI/capita series contributes only 2011-2015, ADF stationarity tests at T = 25 cannot reject unit-root behaviour in either group's education-expenditure share (p = 0.62 for LMC, p = 0.05 for SSA; SSA log GNI is untestable with 5 observations), and the separate-by-group regression on SSA is mechanically over-determined (N = 4, k = 6) so the SSA-specific slope is recovered only through the pooled-with-interaction design.

<workflow>Loaded /workspace/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv (12 indicator-rows x 41 year-columns; two aggregated groups: SSF = Sub-Saharan Africa and LMC = Lower middle income). Reshaped wide to long; restricted to the 1991-2015 window, the only window where the dependent variable (GNI per capita, constant 2015 US$) and all controls are jointly observed for BOTH groups. SSA GNI is observed only 2011-2015, so after first-differencing delta-ln-GNI is available for 24 years in LMC and 4 years in SSA (N = 28). Constructed a Lower-Middle-Income x Educ interaction. Ran ADF stationarity tests (inconclusive at T = 25). Headline model: pooled OLS of delta-ln-GNI on group FE, Educ, D_LMC x Educ, and four controls with Newey-West HAC SE (maxlags = 2). Robustness: separate-by-group (LMC only - SSA over-determined at N = 4, k = 6), levels-with-lagged-DV (rho = 0.90), and exports-growth winsorised at 5 percent / 95 percent per group to neutralise the SSA 1999 (+30.0) and 2011 (-43.3) outliers. Headline interaction: beta(D_LMC x Educ) = +0.078 (NW SE 0.050, p = 0.124). Winsorised-exports robustness interaction: +0.075 (p = 0.151). Levels + lag robustness interaction: +0.088 (p = 0.087).</workflow>
